extracted.intended_audience: students, readers, critics, and writers of American short fiction (anthology/course readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Critical/biographical notes on American short-story writers that imply standards and evaluative criteria for short-story craft (e.g., compression, characterization, economy, atmosphere, point of view). Useful for assessing or teaching short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative power
rubrics_metrics.description: The strength and force of storytelling — the ability of the narrative to move, engage, and command attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as 'narrative power at its best is outstanding' (e.g., Wilbur Daniel Steele). Evaluate whether the story's movement, voice, and sequence produce a commanding effect on the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel settings and atmospheric effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of fresh, original settings and the creation of an effective atmosphere that supports the story's mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steele 'sought novel settings and atmospheric effects'; assess how setting and atmosphere enhance theme and character rather than serving simply as backdrop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression (economy of means)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terseness and economy in language and structure — saying much with little and avoiding unnecessary elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeatedly praised: 'terse-ness', 'utmost economy of means' (Hemingway, William March). Antipattern: verbosity that weakens impact; but note some writers justify measured verbosity for character delineation (Irvin S. Cobb).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delineation of character / characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: The vividness, fidelity, and depth with which characters are drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many notes praise 'rich delineation of character', 'good characterization', 'exact characterization'. Evaluate immediacy, complexity, distinctiveness of characters and whether characterization carries the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between compression and necessary verbosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowing when to compress and when extended detail or 'verbosity' serves characterization or other aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irvin S. Cobb: stories 'would gain greatly by compression, but… privilege of a certain verbosity for the sake of his rich delineation of character.' Score according to whether length serves purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction / structural design
rubrics_metrics.description: The story's structural architecture — how incidents are arranged and how form supports meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frances Gilchrist Wood: 'a feat of construction... very elaborateness of the construction' which can be a danger; evaluate coherence, balance, and whether structure aids or obstructs the reader's experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vitality / human interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The story's life, energy, and capacity to hold human interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'The vitality of the characterization and the sheer human interest' can overcome structural faults; judge immediacy and emotional engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity / first-hand knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy and credibility of depicted worlds based on real knowledge or experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Konrad Bercovici: 'Based on first-hand knowledge and experience' — award stories that show convincing detail grounded in understanding of the subject or culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisp narrative value / freshness
rubrics_metrics.description: A fresh, energetic telling with clear narrative drive and readable phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praiseworthy as 'fresh, crisp narrative value' — avoid languid or stale narration; value immediacy and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmospheric background
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective use of background detail to create mood and support the story's sense of place/time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called out as 'fine atmospheric backgrounds'; evaluate how background detail is integrated and whether it deepens the story's emotional or thematic resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understatement / subtlety
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of restraint and suggestion rather than explicit statement to achieve emotional or intellectual impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hemingway praised for 'emphasis of understatement'; Faulkner for 'indirect implication'. Score how well implication and restraint create depth rather than leaving the reader confused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional and intellectual perception
rubrics_metrics.description: The author's ability to perceive and render subtle emotional and intellectual truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hemingway: stories 'charged most subtly with emotional and intellectual perception' — evaluate insightfulness and the story's capacity to reveal complex interior states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and ear for spoken speech / dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic, convincing dialogue and distinctive narrative voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dorothy Parker ('unusual ear for spoken speech'), Walter D. Edmonds ('fine ear for humorous speech'), George Albee ('ear for folk speech') — judge fidelity and variety in dialogue and its contribution to characterization and realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monologue and spoken-speech handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill in writing extended speech/monologue that remains engaging and revealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parker noted for monologue; evaluate focus, variation, and how monologue reveals character or theme without stalling narrative motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus and unity of impression
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentration on a central effect or impression achieved through coherent selection and arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willa Cather: 'builds up a unity of impression out of several converging strands' — assess whether disparate elements cohere toward a unified effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple perspectives / angle-of-observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of different vantage points or angles to enrich understanding of characters or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cather's 'observed from several angles' — examine whether multiple views strengthen or scatter the story's focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality / observational restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: An objective or neutral presentation that permits readers to draw conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DuBose Heyward: 'impartiality is arresting'; Erskine Caldwell: 'impartial presentation of poor-white life' — measure how restraint clarifies rather than obscures moral stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inevitable quality of drama / dramatic force
rubrics_metrics.description: A sense that events unfold inevitably and with compelling dramatic momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heyward: 'inevitable quality of the drama' and Marquand: 'dramatic force' — look for cause-effect clarity, escalation, and satisfying dramatic logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect implication / point-of-view limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating effect through suggestion and by limiting perspective (e.g., child POV) rather than explicit exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faulkner: 'creating his effects by indirect implication' and conveying truth 'through the half-unrealized perceptions of the children' — assess how POV limitations produce meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony, neatness, and conclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: A controlled ironic tone and a neat, conclusive ending or resolution (or deliberate lack thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dorothy Parker: 'neat, crisp, and conclusive'; Ruth Suckow: 'a little ironic' — determine whether conclusion and tone fit the story's aims; consider when lack of resolution is intentional (Callaghan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of a static situation / observational slice
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing to present a single situation without traditional resolution, inviting reader observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Morley Callaghan: 'take a single static situation and... present it as it is without resolution or comment' — evaluate effectiveness of the observational approach and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic treatment and blending of fantasy with reality
rubrics_metrics.description: A lyrical or poetic style that blends realistic detail with elements of fantasy or poetic imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuel Komroff and Joseph Hergesheimer praised for 'poetic approach' and 'vividly realized fantasy with roots in reality' — assess balance so that poetic/fantastic elements illuminate rather than derail realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural / ethnographic penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Deep, respectful insight into a culture or community different from the author's own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oliver La Farge: 'extraordinary penetration into the reticence of the Indian mind' — value accuracy, sensitivity, and depth of portrayal rather than caricature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice of social critique / period capture
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to capture an era's spirit and offer social or cultural critique through fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F. Scott Fitzgerald: 'typical writer of the jazz age' and social criticism noted — judge how convincingly a story renders its historical moment and social concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor and Rabelaisian anecdote
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of humorous tone or broad, earthy anecdote to characterize scenes or communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: George Milburn: 'chronicler... in brief Rabelaisian anecdote'; assess whether humor serves insight or degenerates into mere caricature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological insight / use of contemporary theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of psychological depth (including contemporary psychological ideas) to illuminate characters' motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hergesheimer anticipates using 'discoveries of Freud' to illuminate probing of reality; evaluate whether psychological layers add believable depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter authenticity and thematic fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching authorial interest and strength to subject matter (e.g., gangster life, poor-white life).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benjamin Appel, Erskine Caldwell: praised for authentic treatment of particular milieus — reward aptness of writer to subject and credible insider detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending revelation / flash revelation impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of quiet narration to build toward a strong, often sudden revelation at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sally Benson: 'quietness of her narration gives special force to the flashing revelation at the end' — judge pacing and payoff of final revelation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone (unpretentiousness / affection / irony)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate tonal stance — unpretentiousness, affection, or ironic distance — that shapes reader response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ruth Suckow: 'unpretentiousness achieves a certain heightened effect'; evaluate whether tone complements character and theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Varied formal innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Willingness to experiment with or invent new short-story forms when successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: William Saroyan 'has invented a new form successfully' — reward formal risks that produce clarity or new expressive means rather than novelty for its own sake.
